learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of mathematics and other basic sciences inherent to their engineering specialty, at a level that allows for the acquisition of the rest of the degree's competencies.

The ability to analyze complex products, processes, and systems in their field of study; to appropriately select and apply established analytical, calculation, and experimental methods, and to correctly interpret the results of such analyses.

Ability to project, design, and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes, and systems specific to their specialty, meeting established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic, and industrial aspects; as well as selecting and applying appropriate project methods.
Knowledge of the application of materials, equipment and tools, technology and engineering processes, and their limitations in their field of expertise.
Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions within the engineering field and with society in general.
Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Model, calculate and examine the static equilibrium of solids.

syllabus_topics: 1.1 Forces and moments. Physical magnitudes. Units. Precision. Scalars and vectors. Vector algebra. Scalar product. Vector product. Forces. Components. Moments and couples of forces. Resultants.
1.2 Newton's Laws. Inertial systems. Newton's laws. Equilibrium of particles and solids.
1.3. Free-body diagrams. Isolation of a mechanical system. Free-body diagrams.
1.4. Centers of gravity. Distributed forces. Centroid. Center of mass. Center of gravity. Distributed forces. Effects on beams.
1.5. Contact forces: normal and friction. Contact forces. Normal force. Static friction. Kinetic friction.
2.1. Rectilinear motion. Velocity and acceleration. Uniformly accelerated accelerated motion. Integration of a(t) and a(v) cases.
2.2. General motion of a particle. Tangential and normal components. Composition of rectilinear motions (2D). Tangential and normal acceleration.
2.3. Practical cases: parabolic motion and circular motion. Parabolic motion: height, range,... Circular motion: angular velocity and acceleration.
2.4. Composition of motions. Relative motion. Composition of velocities.
3.1. Newton's 2nd Law. Inertial mass. Linear momentum. Mechanical impulse. Universal law of gravitation. Gravitational mass. Weight. Inertial forces. Centrifugal force.
3.2. Dynamics of a rigid body. Moment of inertia. Angular momentum. Moment of inertia. Law of rotational dynamics. Rolling.
3.3. Energy methods. Work. Power. Conservative forces. Potential energy. Kinetic energy. Work-energy theorem. Mechanical energy. Conservation of energy.

assessment_methods.method: Individual written and oral tests for evaluating technical competencies
Reports on exercises, case studies, computer practices, simulation practices, and lab practices
Technical ability, involvement in project/PBL, work done, results obtained, documentation delivered, technical presentation, and defense

assessment_rules: Individual written and oral tests for technical competencies include recovery mechanisms. For other assessment components, such as reports on exercises, case studies, and project work (including technical ability, involvement, results, documentation, presentation, and defense), there are no recovery mechanisms.
